not_examined.why: No toolchain installs allowed; analysis is by reading only, all arithmetic worked by hand.
None in fixture; token-behaviour assumptions (fee-on-transfer, hooks, blocklists, rebasing) reasoned about generically.

assumptions.assumption: Only a trusted party can change the price source (pair).
assumptions.counterexample: setPair (L22-24) has no onlyOwner; anyone points it at a contract returning (1, 2^112-1) and borrows the whole debtToken balance against 1 wei collateral.

assumptions.assumption: Pair spot reserves reflect a fair, non-manipulable price.
assumptions.counterexample: Anyone can donate token1 to SimplePair and call public sync(); r1 rises, price() rises linearly, attacker over-borrows within one tx and abandons collateral. Swapping token0 in lowers price and blocks victims' withdrawCollateral.

assumptions.assumption: pair reserve0 is never zero.
assumptions.counterexample: Before the first sync() (reserves start 0) or with a pair set to an empty/reverting contract via the open setPair, price() divides by zero/reverts, and withdrawCollateral calls price() even for users with zero debt -> all collateral frozen until pair fixed (an attacker can keep re-griefing because setPair is permissionless).

assumptions.assumption: Collateral/debt tokens transfer exactly the nominal amount (no fee-on-transfer).
assumptions.counterexample: depositCollateral credits full amount while pool receives less; repay reduces debt by full amount while pool receives less; pool becomes insolvent, last withdrawer reverts.

assumptions.assumption: Undercollateralised positions are resolved somehow.
assumptions.counterexample: No liquidation function exists; once price drops, bad debt is permanent and lenders' debtToken is lost.

assumptions.assumption: borrowers list contains each borrower once and stays small.
assumptions.counterexample: borrow(0) with debtOf==0 pushes msg.sender every call (L40) and passes all checks; array grows without bound, borrowerCount() (O(n) loop) eventually exceeds gas for callers. View-only, so no fund loss.

assumptions.assumption: Token balances fit in uint112.
assumptions.counterexample: sync() silently truncates uint112(balance) (L18-19). Donating token0 so balance = 2^112 + x makes reserve0 = x and price huge; only practical for very low-value / high-supply tokens.

assumptions.assumption: token1.transfer has no callback to the recipient (no reentrancy).
assumptions.counterexample: With a hook-bearing token1 (ERC777-style), swap0For1 transfers token1 before sync(); reentering swap0For1 sees the same in0 (balance-reserve0 unchanged) and old reserves, so the same token0 input satisfies the k-check repeatedly, draining token1.

assumptions.assumption: Input transfer and swap happen atomically.
assumptions.counterexample: If a user transfers token0 in one tx and calls swap0For1 in another, anyone can front-run and consume the excess as their input. Standard Uniswap-style caveat.

assumptions.assumption: Every state-changing entry point checkpoints the user's reward index before changing their stake.
assumptions.counterexample: stake() calls only _updatePool() (L49), not _updateUser(); a fresh staker has userRewardPerTokenPaid=0 and immediately earns staked*rewardPerTokenStored/1e18, i.e. all historical rewards.

assumptions.assumption: Contract holds enough rewardToken for all accrued rewards.
assumptions.counterexample: rewardRate is set without funding check; accruals exceed balance and later claimers' claim() reverts. If rewardToken == stakeToken, rewards are paid out of stakers' principal and last withdrawer cannot exit.

assumptions.assumption: rewardRate * elapsed * 1e18 never overflows.
assumptions.counterexample: An extreme rate makes rewardPerToken() revert; withdraw/claim/stake and even setRewardRate (which calls _updatePool first) revert -> stake permanently frozen. Owner-only misconfiguration, low likelihood.

assumptions.assumption: stakeToken has no fee-on-transfer.
assumptions.counterexample: staked/totalStaked credited at nominal amount; last withdrawer reverts.

assumptions.assumption: withdraw does not depend on reward token health.
Share price cannot be inflated so that deposits round to zero shares.
assumptions.counterexample: First depositor deposits 1 wei, donates D directly; victim depositing < D+1 gets 0 shares (no shares>0 check, L23/L27) and attacker redeems everything.

assumptions.assumption: withdraw(assets) burns at least the fair number of shares (rounds up).
assumptions.counterexample: withdraw computes shares = assets*totalSupply/totalAssets rounded DOWN (L36). When share price > 1 wei, withdraw(assets) with assets*supply < totalAssets burns 0 shares; any address (even with zero balance) receives assets for free, repeatedly.

assumptions.assumption: totalAssets() > 0 whenever totalSupply > 0.
assumptions.counterexample: A negative rebase / slash to 0 balance makes previewDeposit and withdraw divide by zero -> vault bricked for deposits.

assumptions.assumption: asset has no fee-on-transfer.
assumptions.counterexample: Shares are priced on nominal assets before transfer; vault receives less, depositor is over-credited at others' expense.

assumptions.assumption: redeem rounds against the user.
Every recipient transfer always succeeds.
assumptions.counterexample: If any recipient is blocklisted (USDC/USDT), is address(0), or the token reverts on zero-amount transfers for a 0-bps share, distribute() reverts for everyone; recipients are immutable and there is no rescue (owner is unused) -> all funds locked forever.

assumptions.assumption: Recipient list is small enough to loop in one tx.
assumptions.counterexample: Set once at construction; a very long list makes distribute exceed block gas -> permanent lock. Deployer-controlled, low likelihood.

assumptions.assumption: Shares sum to 10000 so balance is fully distributed.

oddities.what: setOwner has onlyOwner, setPair (more critical) has none.
withdraw and claim call _updateUser; stake only calls _updatePool.
redeem rounds assets down (vault-favourable); withdraw rounds shares down (user-favourable) - inconsistent rounding direction.
Calls price() even when debtOf == 0, so a broken/empty oracle freezes debt-free collateral.
Borrower registered before amount/collateral checks; borrow(0) repeatedly duplicates entries.
owner stored but never used; no admin recovery path.
No liquidate function and no lender deposit/withdraw; debt liquidity is presumably sent in directly.

findings.title: Unprotected setPair lets anyone replace the price oracle and drain the pool
findings.mechanism: setPair lacks onlyOwner. price() trusts whatever getReserves() the pair returns.
attack_sequence: Deploy FakePair with getReserves() returning (1, type(uint112).max)
Call LendingPool.setPair(FakePair)
depositCollateral(1)
borrow(debtToken.balanceOf(pool))
Optionally setPair back to original to hide
findings.impact: Theft of all debtToken in the pool; also allows freezing all collateral by setting a reverting pair.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test: non-owner calls setPair with mock, borrows full balance; assert pool debtToken balance == 0.

findings.title: New stakers claim all historical rewards because stake() does not checkpoint the user
findings.mechanism: stake() updates the pool index but never sets userRewardPerTokenPaid[msg.sender]; earned() then multiplies the new stake by the full (rewardPerToken - 0) (or by the delta since an older checkpoint for top-ups).
attack_sequence: Wait until rewardPerTokenStored is large
Attacker stakes a large amount (can be flash-borrowed)
Attacker calls claim() in the same tx -> earned = amount*rewardPerTokenStored/1e18
withdraw(amount) and repay flash loan
preconditions: Pool has accrued rewards (rewardPerTokenStored > 0) and holds rewardToken
findings.impact: Theft of the entire reward balance; honest stakers' claims revert afterwards.
findings.how_to_validate: Test: Alice stakes, warp 1 day, Bob stakes same amount and claims immediately; Bob's payout equals Alice's full accrued reward.

findings.title: ShareVault.withdraw rounds shares burned down, letting anyone withdraw assets for zero shares
findings.mechanism: shares = assets*totalSupply/totalAssets floors; when totalAssets > totalSupply, choosing assets < totalAssets/totalSupply burns 0 shares; balanceOf[sender] -= 0 succeeds for any address.
attack_sequence: Precondition: share price > 1 asset-wei per share (yield, donation, or inflation)
Attacker with no shares calls withdraw(floor((totalAssets-1)/totalSupply)) repeatedly
Each call transfers assets and burns 0 shares
findings.impact: Drain of vault assets; with an inflated vault (supply=1, assets=1e18+1) a single call steals ~all assets.
findings.how_to_validate: Test: deposit 1 wei, donate 1e18, from a fresh address call withdraw(1e18); assert it succeeds and fresh address receives 1e18.

findings.title: First-depositor share inflation makes later deposits mint zero shares
findings.mechanism: totalAssets uses raw balanceOf (donations count), previewDeposit floors, and deposit does not require shares > 0.
attack_sequence: Attacker deposit(1) on empty vault -> 1 share
Attacker transfers D asset directly to vault
Victim deposit(X) with X <= D -> shares = X*1/(D+1) = 0
Attacker redeem(1) -> receives D+1+X
preconditions: Vault empty or tiny supply; attacker front-runs a deposit
findings.how_to_validate: Test the sequence above; assert victim shares == 0 and attacker balance gain == X.

findings.title: Spot-price oracle from SimplePair is manipulable via donation + public sync
findings.mechanism: price = r1/r0 read instantaneously; anyone can raise r1 by sending token1 to the pair and calling sync().
attack_sequence: Flash-borrow token1 D and token0 C with C > (4/3)*r0
depositCollateral(C)
Transfer D token1 to pair, call pair.sync()
borrow(0.75*C*(r1+D)/r0), up to pool liquidity
Partially recover donation by swapping token0 in via swap0For1, repay flash loans, abandon collateral
preconditions: Thin pair liquidity relative to attacker capital; pool holds significant debtToken
findings.impact: Pool drained beyond true collateral value (net profit D*(0.75C/r0 - 1) - 0.25*C*r1/r0 before donation recovery). Downward manipulation (swap0For1) temporarily blocks victims' withdrawCollateral.
findings.how_to_validate: Fork-style unit test with small pair reserves; compute attacker net balance change across the sequence.

findings.title: Single failing recipient permanently locks PayoutSplitter funds
findings.mechanism: All transfers in one loop with require; recipients immutable; no skip/pull pattern or rescue.
attack_sequence: Token issuer blocklists one recipient (or recipient is address(0), or a 0-bps share hits a token that reverts on zero-value transfer)
Every distribute() call reverts
preconditions: Token with blocklist / zero-transfer revert / zero-address revert
findings.impact: Permanent lock of all present and future funds for all recipients.
findings.how_to_validate: Mock token reverting on transfer to one address; assert distribute reverts and no other path moves funds.

findings.title: Empty or reverting oracle freezes debt-free collateral withdrawals
findings.mechanism: withdrawCollateral always calls price(); r0 == 0 (pair never synced) or a reverting pair (via open setPair) causes revert even when debtOf == 0.
attack_sequence: Attacker calls setPair(RevertingPair)
All withdrawCollateral calls revert; attacker re-sets after any fix (front-running setPair)
preconditions: Open setPair (see finding 1) or unsynced pair
findings.impact: Collateral blocked for as long as the griefer persists; recoverable only by out-racing them.
findings.how_to_validate: Test: deposit, setPair to mock with reserves (0,0), withdrawCollateral reverts.

findings.title: Reentrant swap0For1 reuses the same input with callback-bearing token1
findings.mechanism: token1.transfer occurs before sync(), no lock; reentrant call recomputes in0 against stale reserve0 and k against stale reserves.
attack_sequence: Send in0 token0 to pair
swap0For1(out, attackerContract)
In token1 transfer hook, call swap0For1(out, attackerContract) again; repeat while token1 balance >= out
findings.impact: Drain of pair token1 reserves; also corrupts LendingPool price.
findings.how_to_validate: Mock ERC777-style token1 with recipient callback; assert multiple outputs for one input.

findings.title: Unfunded or same-token rewards make RewardPool insolvent
findings.mechanism: Rate set with no balance check; if stakeToken == rewardToken claims consume principal.
attack_sequence: Rate set higher than funding
Early claimers drain rewardToken; with same token, principal is paid out and last withdraw reverts
findings.how_to_validate: Deploy with s == r, small funding; claim then attempt full withdraw of all stakers.

findings.title: Fee-on-transfer tokens over-credit deposits across LendingPool, RewardPool and ShareVault
findings.mechanism: Credited amount is the nominal argument, not the received balance delta.
attack_sequence: Use a fee-on-transfer token as the asset
Deposit/repay repeatedly; credited > received
Withdraw full credited amount, leaving others short
findings.how_to_validate: Mock 1% fee token; deposit then full withdraw by two users, second reverts.

notes: Highest-severity, high-confidence issues: open setPair (LendingPool), missing user checkpoint in RewardPool.stake, ShareVault.withdraw rounding and first-depositor inflation. Low-impact: borrow(0) inflates borrowers array (view-only DoS); uint112 truncation in SimplePair.sync needs >2^112 units. Rewards during totalStaked==0 periods are silently stranded (not stolen). Token-behaviour findings depend on token choice, which the fixture does not pin down. All conclusions from static reading; no tests were run.
